subject: Learning Methods
title: Chronotypes: Larks and Owls
description: A quick, practical guide to Chronotypes: Larks and Owls.

hook.text: About 25 % of people are morning larks, 25 % are night owls, and 50 % fall in between. Chronotype is largely genetic.

buildup.text: Your chronotype determines your peak alertness window. Larks peak in the morning.

discovery.text: Students who studied during their peak chronotype window scored markedly higher than those who studied at off-peak.

twist.text: Schools start early, forcing owls to learn at their worst time. This mismatch alone can cost owls a full letter grade.

climax.text: Identify your natural peak. Schedule your hardest learning during that window. Save routine tasks for off-peak hours.

punchline.text: Know your peak. Schedule hard learning there. Chronotype matters.

quiz.question: How does studying during your off-peak chronotype window affect performance?
options: It has no measurable effect on scores
It can lower performance by the equivalent of a full letter grade
It improves memory because the brain works harder
